newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Workers break picket lines at S.Korea's Hyundai.
newsitem.headline: Workers break picket lines at S.Korea's Hyundai.

text.p: Several hundred non-union workers broke through picket lines at South Korea's Hyundai Heavy Industries on Wednesday in defiance of a strike billed as the biggest in history, witnesses said.
They said the workers scuffled briefly with about 300 unionists who had blocked the entrance to South Korea's largest shipyard, which was now operating normally.

In Seoul, a Labour Ministry official said essential services had not been affected by a nationwide strike call from two trade unions in protest at a controversial labour law that has sparked three weeks of wildcat stoppages.
"Korea Telecom, the postal service and the nation's railroad services have not been influenced by the strike," he said.
Subway trains, buses and taxis shuttled residents to work with little delay.

The Federation of Korean Trade Unions had called for a two-day "all-out" strike starting on Tuesday and the rival Korean Confederation of Trade Unions had ordered public sector workers under its control to stop work from Wednesday.
